attributes.body_ja:
「次第（しだい）」は、どのような語（ご）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われるかで、意味（いみ）が変（か）わる名詞（めいし）です。ここでは、ふつうの動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）やスル動詞（どうし）の語幹（ごかん）とつながる「次第（しだい）」の使（かた）い方（かた）を学（まな）びます。「次第（しだい）」そのものは名詞（めいし）ですが、この「次第（しだい）」は接尾語（せつびご）のように扱（あつか）われます。

基本的（きほんてき）に、この「次第（しだい）」は「(A) のあとすぐに」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「次第（しだい）」には、いくつかの意味（いみ）がありま すが、どれも「(A) によって (B) が決（き）まる」ことを表（あらわ）しており、「物事（ものごと）の進（すす）み方（かた）を決（き）める」という意味（いみ）で共通（きょうつう）しています。

動詞（どうし） + 次第（しだい） - 動詞（どうし）そのものは、何（なに）かを決（き）める力（ちから）を持（も）たないので、「(A) が起（お）こったら (B) が起（お）こる」という意味（いみ）になる。

生（い）き物（もの）の名詞（めいし） + 次第（しだい） - 生（い）き物（もの）には何（なに）かを決（き）める力（ちから）があるので、「(A) の行動（こうどう）や判断（はんだん）によって、(B) が決（き）まる」という意味（いみ）になる。

生（い）き物（もの）以外（いがい）の名詞（めいし）・具体性（ぐたいせい）のない名詞（めいし） + 次第（しだい） - このような名詞（めいし）には何（なに）かを決（き）める力（ちから）はないので、「(A) の条件（じょうけん）や状況（じょうきょう）によって、(B) が決（き）まる」という意味（いみ）になる。(B) には判断（はんだん）のような内容（ないよう）が入（はい）ることが多（おお）い。
attributes.body:
次第（しだい） is a noun that is often translated in different ways, depending on what type of word it follows. In this lesson, we will look at the meaning associated with the conjunctive form of standard verbs, and the stem of する verbs. Although it is a noun, 次第（しだい） may also be classified simply as a suffix in many cases.

Basically, 次第（しだい） means 'next in sequence after (A)', and is often translated to 'as soon as (A)'.

Fun Fact

One of the most important things to keep in mind with 次第（しだい）, is that the literal meaning in almost every situation is 'determining sequence'. This is unlike any standard phrase in English, but simply expresses that (A) is what will govern (B). Let's look at how this translates with different word types.

Verb 次第（しだい） - Verb determines the sequence of (B). Since a verb is not capable of making a choice, (A) simply 'happening' will result in (B).

Living noun 次第（しだい） - Noun determines the sequence of (B). Since living things can make choices, (B) will depend on (A).

Inanimate/abstract noun 次第（しだい） - Noun determines the sequence of (B). Since inanimate/abstract things cannot make choices, (A) will determine (B)'s course of action. (B) will usually involve some kind of decision.

attributes.body: Both describe how one thing leads to another, but with different nuance. 次第 emphasizes immediacy, e.g. 方法が決まり次第連絡します ('I'll contact you as soon as the method is decided.') によって・による shows variation or dependence, e.g. 方法によって結果が変わる ('The result changes depending on the method.')

second_relatable.title: によって・による
second_relatable.meaning: By means of, According to, Depending on, Because of, Due to

attributes.body: Both describe sequences where one action quickly follows another, but differ in tone and formality. 次第 is formal and indicates that an action will follow as soon as another is completed, e.g. '会議が終わり次第、報告します' ('I'll report as soon as the meeting ends'). たとたんに emphasizes sudden or unexpected results, often in conversation, e.g. 'ドアを開けたとたんに猫が飛び出した' ('The moment I opened the door, the cat jumped out').

second_relatable.title: たとたんに
second_relatable.meaning: The instant or moment, As soon as, Just as

attributes.body: 次第 emphasizes timing or sequencing, used to express that one action is a condition for the next, which will follow immediately. For example, 準備ができ次第出発します ('As soon as preparations are done, we'll depart'). にかかわる focuses on relevance or importance, describing how something affects or relates to another matter. For example, 命にかかわる問題 ('a matter of life').

second_relatable.title: にかかわる
second_relatable.meaning: To relate to, To have to do with, Concerning, Depends on

attributes.body: Both of these expressions use 次第 but differ slightly in usage. 次第 alone attaches to verb stems to emphasize timing or sequencing, expressing that one action is a condition for the next. For example, 終わり次第連絡します ('I'll contact you as soon as I'm finished'). 次第だ・次第で, by contrast, introduces conditional relationships or dependence. For example, 努力次第で結果は変わる ('The results will depend on your effort').

Both なり and 次第 indicate immediacy but differ in tone and nuance. なり is a neutral expression suggesting a spontaneous or automatic reaction. For example, 布団に入るなり寝た ('He fell asleep as soon as he got in his futon'). 次第 has a more formal tone and is often used in business contexts to show that something happens immediately after a condition is met. For example, 終わり次第ご連絡します ('I'll contact you as soon as I'm finished').

first_relatable.title: なり
first_relatable.meaning: As soon as, The moment, When

attributes.body: Both 直ちに and 次第 can imply prompt timing, but differ in grammatical usage and nuance. 直ちに is used before phrases and emphasizes urgency, e.g. '直ちに避難してください' ('Please evacuate immediately'). 次第 attaches to verb stems to suggest one action happening immediately after another, e.g. '準備ができ次第、出発します' ('We'll leave as soon as we're ready').

first_relatable.title: 直ちに
first_relatable.meaning: At once, Immediately, As soon as
